## Self-testing: test hunks: 2 (the middle one)

The checker applies **hunk 2 (E3, the new self-test checks) ALONE at the tip, and `--self-test` must go RED (exit 12)**. Then it applies **hunks 1 and 3 (E1, E2, the fix) on top, and it must go GREEN (exit 0)**. Keep the file order: E1 (`@@ -429`), E3 (`@@ -628`), E2 (`@@ -792`).

## What is wrong (one paragraph)

QA F-5 (PR #793) stopped a FUTURE vulnerability-DB timestamp from printing as "0.0h old" inside a CLEARED verdict. It has two halves: the PRODUCER (`:797-:831`, an inline `python3 -c` inside a `$( docker run ... )` command substitution, which prints `future` for a stamp ahead of the clock) and the CONSUMER (`decide()`'s `if db_age_future:` arm at `:382`). The self-test can only red the consumer: `run_case` (`:447-:466`) calls `decide "$tmp/report" "$ref" "$age" 72` with the age passed in **as a string** (`:452`), so no case ever runs the producer. The ticket, verbatim: "restoring `print(f"{max(age, 0.0):.2f}")` in the producer leaves the self-test at **20 PASS / 0 FAIL**". Its Done-means: (1) extract the age computation into a shell function the self-test can call with a synthetic trivy stamp; (2) a case pair, future stamp -> `future`, normal stamp -> numeric age; (3) red-proof: restoring the clamp reds case 1 and leaves case 2 green. This task does exactly that. E1 moves the producer's python, byte for byte, into a new function `db_age_from_version_json()` defined above `self_test()`. E2 makes the main flow call it. E3 adds the two producer checks to `self_test()`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Base-image watch GATE (KS-365) — the replacement for the dead monthly cron
# =============================================================================
# WHY THIS EXISTS
#
# KS-365's watch was `.github/workflows/base-image-refresh.yml`, cron
# "0 2 1 * *". Its last run was 2026-08-01; the 2026-09-01 run never fired,
# because GitHub Actions stopped starting jobs on 2026-08-17 and Kam decided on
# 2026-08-27 not to restore it. That is a decided state, not an outage, so
# nothing re-arms by itself.
#
# The important part is WHICH half died. `deployment/azure/refresh-base-images.sh`
# still pulls and still scans — it reports, and NEVER GATES ON FINDINGS. (It can
# exit non-zero for its own reasons: `set -euo pipefail` plus an ERR trap, a
# wrong-tenant `exit 1`, `exit 64` on a bad option. What it will not do is fail
# because a scan found something — QA F-9 corrected the earlier "always exits
# 0", which overstated it.) The two FAILURE
# CONDITIONS that made the report actionable lived in the workflow, not in the
# script. So when the cron stopped, the scanner survived and the GATE vanished,
# which is the worst of the two to lose silently: the scan still tells you the
# truth, and nobody is listening.
#
# This script is that gate, moved into the repo where it can be run by hand.
# It deliberately does NOT re-implement pulling: it calls the existing script's
# credential-free `local` leg for that (digest before/after, MOVED reporting),
# because two copies of the pull logic is how they drift apart.
#
# USAGE
#   ./base-image-watch.sh              # pull + scan + gate  (the monthly run)
#   ./base-image-watch.sh --scan-only  # gate the images already local (no pull)
#   ./base-image-watch.sh --self-test  # positive control; runs no docker at all
#
# What --self-test actually checks, stated because the count has been quoted
# loosely before (QA F-14): 15 `run_case` verdict cases + 2 structural checks
# (the base list is in step with refresh-base-images.sh; every derived image is
# accounted for) + 1 parse check (`bash -n` on this file) = 18 PASS lines.
#
# EXIT CODES — every non-zero one is a human's cue, and they are distinct on
# purpose so a caller can tell "act now" from "something broke".
#   0   status quo: only the baselined residual is present. Nothing to do.
#   10  THE RESIDUAL CLEARED. postgres:15-alpine reports 0 CRITICAL, so the
#       upstream rebuild landed. Run `refresh-base-images.sh acr` (needs the
#       Founders Hub login) and close KS-365's residual.
#   11  AN UNEXPECTED CRITICAL. A pinned base re-accumulated a critical CVE.
#       Treat like KS-363: refresh/bump the base, rebuild, redeploy.
#   12  self-test failed — the gate cannot be trusted; fix it before believing
#       any run.
#   2   environment problem (docker or the repo layout), not a finding.
#   64  unknown command-line option.
#   1   anything bash itself failed on under `set -euo pipefail`. Not a verdict:
#       if you see 1, the gate did not reach one. (Listed because QA/review found
#       a path that produced a bare 1 with no output — now fixed; it is still
#       reachable in principle, and an undocumented code reads as "broken" with
#       no diagnosis.)
#
# WHAT IS GATED, AND WHAT IS ONLY REPORTED
#   CRITICAL findings are what this gate decides on. HIGH findings are counted
#   and PRINTED for context and are deliberately NOT gated — pgbouncer alone
#   carries ~40, and gating them would make this a permanent red rather than a
#   signal. So "0 CRITICAL / 40 HIGH ... Nothing to do." is the intended
#   reading, not an oversight (QA F-3b: that scope was previously left to
#   silence).
#
#   A verdict of "cleared" additionally requires PROOF THE SCAN ENUMERATED
#   SOMETHING — result groups and total findings both non-zero. An empty report
#   and a stale vulnerability DB both produce "0 CRITICAL" while proving
#   nothing, and both used to read as cleared (QA F-5 / review item 3).
#
# ⚠ ON "EXIT NON-ZERO ON ANY CRITICAL"
#   This script does NOT do that, and the deviation is deliberate. postgres's
#   CVE-2025-68121 has been present continuously since 2026-08 and is not ours
#   to fix — it is Go stdlib vendored into the image's `gosu` binary, and it is
#   identical in postgres 15/16/17, so no bump clears it. A gate that goes red
#   on it goes red every single month forever, and a permanent red is read as
#   noise and then ignored — at which point a REAL critical arrives and lands in
#   a channel everyone has learned to skip. So the one known residual is
#   baselined by exact (image, CVE) pair below, and its DISAPPEARANCE is what
#   raises the alarm (exit 10) because that is the actionable moment.
#   Anything outside that pair is exit 11. Nothing is silently tolerated: the
#   baseline is one line, it is printed on every run, and the self-test proves
#   it cannot be widened by accident.
# =============================================================================

REFERENCE_IMAGE="${REFERENCE_IMAGE:-alpine:3.10}"
# How stale the vulnerability DB may be before the run is refused, in hours.

MAX_DB_AGE_HOURS="${MAX_DB_AGE_HOURS:-72}"

# --- the analysis, isolated so the self-test can drive it without docker ------
# Reads trivy JSON on stdin, prints the human verdict line, and appends the
# machine-readable "<image>|<crit>|<cves>" row to the file named by $2.
analyse_json() {
    local img="$1" rowfile="$2"
    python3 -c '
import json, sys

img = sys.argv[1]
baseline_cve = sys.argv[2]
data = json.load(sys.stdin)

crit = high = 0
# QA F-5 / Peter review item 3: the vacuous-green control in decide() covers a
# MISSING row, not an EMPTY one. Nothing here proved the scan enumerated
# anything, so valid-but-empty trivy JSON on the baselined image read as
# `crit == 0` => "THE RESIDUAL CLEARED" => exit 10, whose printed remedy sends
# an operator at the LIVE Founders Hub registry. A false ACTIONABLE is the more
# expensive direction on this gate. These two counters are the liveness proof:
# `groups` is how many result groups trivy returned, `total` how many findings
# it reported across all scanned severities. decide() refuses to call anything
# "cleared" unless both are non-zero.
groups = 0
total = 0
cves = set()
# The two detail fields KS-365 kept having to be re-derived by hand: the Go
# stdlib version vendored into the image helper binary, and the alpine openssl
# package version. Surfacing them means the next reader does not re-run trivy
# just to answer "how far behind is it".
gosu_stdlib = None
openssl_pkg = None

for result in data.get("Results") or []:
    groups += 1
    total += len(result.get("Vulnerabilities") or [])
    target = result.get("Target") or ""
    for vuln in result.get("Vulnerabilities") or []:
        sev = vuln.get("Severity")
        if sev == "CRITICAL":
            crit += 1
            cves.add(vuln.get("VulnerabilityID", "?"))
        elif sev == "HIGH":
            high += 1
        pkg = vuln.get("PkgName")
        installed = vuln.get("InstalledVersion")
        if pkg == "stdlib" and "gosu" in target:
            gosu_stdlib = installed
        if pkg in ("libcrypto3", "libssl3") and openssl_pkg is None:
            openssl_pkg = installed

line = f"  {img}: {crit} CRITICAL / {high} HIGH"
if cves:
    line += " — criticals: " + ", ".join(sorted(cves))
detail = []
if gosu_stdlib:
    detail.append(f"gosu stdlib {gosu_stdlib}")
if openssl_pkg:
    detail.append(f"openssl {openssl_pkg}")
if detail:
    line += "\n      (" + "; ".join(detail) + ")"
print(line)

joined = ",".join(sorted(cves))
with open(sys.argv[3], "a") as fd:
    fd.write(f"{img}|{crit}|{joined}|{groups}|{total}\n")
' "$img" "$BASELINE_CVE" "$rowfile"
}

# --- verdict -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Given the collected per-image results, decide the exit code. Pure function of
# its inputs: the self-test drives it directly.
#   $1 = path to a file of "<image>|<crit>|<cves>" lines
decide() {
    local report="$1"
    # QA F-4's currency control. Defaulted so the self-test can drive decide()
    # without docker: an empty reference means "no control was run", which the
    # judge treats as INDETERMINATE rather than as a pass.
    local ref_image="${2:-}"
    local db_age="${3:-}"
    local max_db_age="${4:-72}"
    python3 -c '
import sys

report_path, baseline_image, baseline_cve = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
# QA F-4. Both are the CURRENCY control; the caller measures them, this only judges.
reference_image = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else ""
# QA F-5: "future" is a THIRD state, distinct from unreadable (-1) and from any
# real age. It is carried as its own sentinel so decide() can give it its own
# message; collapsing it into either of the other two is what produced the
# "0.0h old" clearance.
_raw_age = sys.argv[5] if len(sys.argv) > 5 else ""
db_age_future = _raw_age == "future"
db_age_hours = float(_raw_age) if _raw_age not in ("", "unknown", "future") else -1.0
max_db_age_hours = float(sys.argv[6]) if len(sys.argv) > 6 else 72.0
rows = []
for raw in open(report_path):
    raw = raw.strip()
    if not raw:
        continue
    parts = raw.split("|")
    if len(parts) < 5:
        # A row without the liveness fields cannot be judged. Refusing beats
        # guessing on the one gate whose false-positive costs real work.
        print(f"VERDICT: malformed report row (expected 5 fields, got {len(parts)}): {raw}")
        sys.exit(11)
    image, crit, cves, groups, total = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], parts[3], parts[4]
    rows.append((image, int(crit), [c for c in cves.split(",") if c], int(groups), int(total)))

unexpected = []
residual_seen = False
residual_cleared = False
# QA F-4: did the control image report the severity this gate acts on?
reference_criticals = None
for image, crit, cves, groups, total in rows:
    if reference_image and image == reference_image:
        reference_criticals = crit

vacuous = []

for image, crit, cves, groups, total in rows:
    if reference_image and image == reference_image:
        continue
    # QA F-5 / Peter item 3. `crit == 0` means "cleared" ONLY if the scan
    # actually enumerated something. An empty-but-valid report (groups == 0) and
    # a stale-vuln-DB report that finds nothing at all (total == 0) both produce
    # `crit == 0` while proving nothing, and both used to reach exit 10 —
    # sending an operator to `az acr import --force` against the live registry.
    if crit == 0 and (groups == 0 or total == 0):
        vacuous.append((image, groups, total))

for image, crit, cves, groups, total in rows:
    if image == baseline_image:
        if baseline_cve in cves:
            residual_seen = True
        elif crit == 0 and groups > 0 and total > 0:
            residual_cleared = True
        # A critical on the baselined image that is NOT the baselined CVE is
        # still unexpected — the baseline is an (image, CVE) pair, not a
        # blanket pass for that image.
        for c in cves:
            if c != baseline_cve:
                unexpected.append((image, c))
    elif reference_image and image == reference_image:
        # The control is not one of our bases — its criticals are the POINT, not
        # a finding. Judging them here would red every run by construction.
        pass
    else:
        for c in cves:
            unexpected.append((image, c))

if vacuous:
    print("VERDICT: THE SCAN ENUMERATED NOTHING — treating as a broken run, not a pass.")
    for image, groups, total in vacuous:
        print(f"  {image}: 0 CRITICAL, but {groups} result group(s) and {total} finding(s) —")
        print("      a clean report and an empty one are indistinguishable without this check.")
    print("Action: check the trivy vulnerability DB is current and the image resolved, then re-run.")
    print("Do NOT run the ACR leg on this result.")
    sys.exit(11)

if unexpected:
    print("VERDICT: UNEXPECTED CRITICAL — a pinned base has re-accumulated a critical CVE.")
    for image, c in unexpected:
        print(f"  {image}: {c}")
    print("Action: refresh or bump that base, rebuild, redeploy (the KS-363 shape).")
    sys.exit(11)

# QA F-4. A "cleared" verdict sends an operator at the live registry with
# `az acr import --force`, so it is the one verdict that must not be reachable
# on an un-current scan. Both controls are checked BEFORE it, and either one
# missing makes the run INDETERMINATE — which is not the same as "still there"
# and emphatically not the same as "cleared".
if residual_cleared:
    indeterminate = []
    # QA F-6. These arms were BOTH guarded on `reference_image` being truthy, so
    # an empty reference appended nothing and the control silently disappeared —
    # a cleared verdict then reached exit 10 printing "reported None CRITICAL",
    # which is the opposite of what the comment above claims. An absent control
    # is not a passed control. Unreachable through the shipped entry point (the
    # `:-` default at the top supplies a reference), but reachable from the
    # self-test and from any refactor, and this is the one verdict that sends an
    # operator at the live registry with `az acr import --force`.
    if not reference_image:
        indeterminate.append(
            "CURRENCY: no reference image was supplied, so no control was run — nothing "
            "establishes that this run can see criticals at all")
    elif reference_criticals is None:
        indeterminate.append(
            f"the control image {reference_image} produced no row — it was not scanned, "
            "so nothing establishes that this run can see criticals at all")
    elif reference_criticals == 0:
        indeterminate.append(
            f"the control image {reference_image} reported 0 CRITICAL. It is EOL and pinned, so "
            "either the vulnerability DB cannot see criticals in this run, or the control has "
            "rotted. Both mean a 0 on the baselined image proves nothing.")
    if db_age_future:
        print("VERDICT: INDETERMINATE [CURRENCY] — the vulnerability DB timestamp is in the FUTURE.")
        print("  A future stamp means the clock or the cache cannot be trusted, so the DB age")
        print("  is unreadable — NOT fresh. This is refused rather than reported as 0.0h old,")
        print("  which is what it used to print inside a CLEARED verdict.")
        print("Action: fix the host clock or discard the secuura-trivy-cache volume, then re-run.")
        print("Do NOT run the ACR leg on this result.")
        sys.exit(11)
    if db_age_hours < 0:
        indeterminate.append(
            "the vulnerability DB age could not be read from the trivy metadata")
    elif db_age_hours > max_db_age_hours:
        indeterminate.append(
            f"the vulnerability DB is {db_age_hours:.1f}h old (limit {max_db_age_hours:.0f}h)")
    if indeterminate:
        # QA F-7. Exit 11 is FIVE different verdicts (malformed row, vacuous
        # scan, unexpected critical, this one, missing baseline row), so the
        # four currency cases asserting the CODE alone would pass on any of
        # them. This marker gives the currency verdict an identity of its own,
        # and the cases assert the LINE, not just the code. (The word "verdict"
        # is deliberately not possessive here: this block is python inside a
        # SINGLE-QUOTED bash string, and an apostrophe closes it — the trap that
        # broke this script once already.)
        print("VERDICT: INDETERMINATE [CURRENCY] — the residual LOOKS cleared, but this run cannot prove it.")
        for line in indeterminate:
            print(f"  - {line}")
        print("A clean CRITICAL count and a blind CRITICAL scan are indistinguishable without")
        print("a control for the severity the gate acts on. Refusing to call this cleared.")
        print("Action: re-download the vulnerability DB (trivy image --download-db-only")
        print("        against the same secuura-trivy-cache volume), then re-run.")
        print("Do NOT run the ACR leg on this result.")
        sys.exit(11)
    print(f"VERDICT: THE RESIDUAL CLEARED — {baseline_image} no longer reports {baseline_cve}.")
    print(f"  Currency control: {reference_image} reported {reference_criticals} CRITICAL "
          f"and the vulnerability DB is {db_age_hours:.1f}h old — so this run CAN see criticals.")
    print("Action: the upstream rebuild landed. Run")
    print("  ./deployment/azure/refresh-base-images.sh acr    (needs the Founders Hub login)")
    print("then close the KS-365 residual.")
    sys.exit(10)

if residual_seen:
    print(f"VERDICT: status quo — {baseline_image} still carries {baseline_cve} (upstream Go stdlib in")
    print("the image gosu binary; identical in postgres 15/16/17, so no bump clears it). Nothing to do.")
    sys.exit(0)

print("VERDICT: the baselined residual was neither present nor cleared — the scan did not")
print(f"produce a row for {baseline_image} at all. Treating as a broken run, not a pass.")
sys.exit(11)
' "$report" "$BASELINE_IMAGE" "$BASELINE_CVE" "$ref_image" "$db_age" "$max_db_age"
}

# --- self-test: the positive control -----------------------------------------
# The whole point is that this gate must not be able to pass vacuously. Each
# case asserts an EXIT CODE, and the first two are known-bad inputs that MUST
# fail. If the gate ever stops failing on them it is broken, and this says so.
self_test() {
    local tmp exp got fails=0
    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' RETURN

    # QA F-4: the currency control is passed through, so a case can drive decide()
    # WITH a working control (arg 4/5) or deliberately WITHOUT one (omit them).
    # QA F-7: $6 is an optional substring the OUTPUT must contain. Exit 11 is
    # five different verdicts, so a case asserting the code alone passes on any
    # of them — the currency cases now name the verdict they mean.
    run_case() {
        local name="$1" expected="$2" body="$3"
        local ref="${4-}" age="${5-}" want_line="${6-}"
        printf '%s\n' "$body" > "$tmp/report"
        set +e
        decide "$tmp/report" "$ref" "$age" 72 > "$tmp/out" 2>&1
        got=$?
        set -e
        if [ "$got" -ne "$expected" ]; then
            echo "  FAIL  $name — expected exit $expected, got $got"
            sed 's/^/          /' "$tmp/out"
            fails=$((fails + 1))
        elif [ -n "$want_line" ] && ! grep -qF "$want_line" "$tmp/out"; then
            echo "  FAIL  $name — exit $got was right, but the verdict line was not '$want_line'"
            sed 's/^/          /' "$tmp/out"
            fails=$((fails + 1))
        else
            echo "  PASS  $name (exit $got)"
        fi
    }
    # The currency verdict's marker, asserted by the FIVE cases below.
    # QA F-6: this said "four". It was five even then, and the miscount is the
    # kind that makes a reader stop looking for the fifth.
    local CURRENCY_LINE="VERDICT: INDETERMINATE [CURRENCY]" 

    # QA F-14. `bash -n` ran NOWHERE automatically, and this file is python
    # embedded in SINGLE-QUOTED bash strings — where one apostrophe in prose
    # closes the string and breaks the whole script, with the error pointing
    # dozens of lines from the edit. It has happened here once already. Parsing
    # is now the first thing the self-test does, so a syntax error is caught by
    # the gate rather than by the next person to run it.
    echo "=== self-test: the script parses ==="
    if bash -n "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" 2>"$tmp/parse"; then
        echo "  PASS  bash -n clean"
    else
        echo "  FAIL  bash -n rejected this script:"
        sed 's/^/          /' "$tmp/parse"
        fails=$((fails + 1))
    fi

    echo "=== self-test: the gate must FAIL on known-bad input ==="

    # Rows are "<image>|<crit>|<cves>|<groups>|<findings>". The last two are the
    # liveness proof added for QA F-5: a real scan of these bases returns
    # several result groups and dozens of HIGH findings, so non-zero values are
    # what a genuine run looks like.

    # 1. POSITIVE CONTROL — a critical on a non-baselined base must fail.
    run_case "unexpected critical on node -> 11" 11 \
"node:24-alpine|1|CVE-2026-59873|3|22
postgres:15-alpine|1|$BASELINE_CVE|3|41"

    # 2. POSITIVE CONTROL — the residual clearing is the actionable moment.
    #
    #    QA F-4 CHANGED THIS CASE, and the change is the finding. These two rows
    #    used to be the whole input, and `postgres:15-alpine|0||3|40` reached
    #    exit 10 "cleared" on `groups > 0 and total > 0` alone. But the scan runs
    #    --severity CRITICAL,HIGH, so those 40 findings can be entirely HIGHs
    #    while the CRITICAL answer is missing because the DB is too old to know
    #    — enumeration, not currency. The bare input is now INDETERMINATE and
    #    has its own case below ("control was never scanned"). To still assert
    #    what this case is FOR, it supplies a working currency control.
    run_case "residual cleared on postgres, with a working currency control -> 10" 10 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||3|40
alpine:3.10|7|CVE-A,CVE-B|4|31" "alpine:3.10" "2.0"

    # 3. The status quo must pass — otherwise the gate is a permanent red.
    run_case "status quo -> 0" 0 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|1|$BASELINE_CVE|3|41"

    # 4. The baseline is an (image, CVE) PAIR, not a free pass for the image.
    run_case "different critical on the baselined image -> 11" 11 \
"postgres:15-alpine|1|CVE-2099-00000|3|41"

    # 5. A scan that produced no row for the baselined image is a broken run,
    #    not a pass — the failure mode that makes a green meaningless.
    run_case "baselined image missing from the report -> 11" 11 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22"

    # 5a. QA F-5 — an EMPTY but structurally valid report. Case 5 covers a
    #     MISSING row; this is the row that is present and says nothing. Before
    #     the fix this reached exit 10 and sent an operator at the live ACR.
    run_case "empty scan on the baselined image -> 11 (not 10)" 11 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||0|0"

    # 5b. Peter review item 3 — a STALE vulnerability DB. trivy warns on stderr,
    #     still emits valid JSON with its result groups intact, and reports no
    #     findings. Structurally different from 5a (groups > 0), same false
    #     "cleared" before the fix.
    run_case "stale vuln DB on the baselined image -> 11 (not 10)" 11 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||3|0"

    # 5c. NEGATIVE CONTROL for 5a/5b — the liveness fields must not be able to
    #     turn a genuine clearance into a red. Same rows as case 2, now with a
    #     WORKING currency control (QA F-4): the reference reports 7 criticals
    #     and the DB is 2h old, so the run demonstrably can see criticals.
    run_case "a LIVE scan WITH a working currency control still reaches cleared -> 10" 10 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||5|61
alpine:3.10|7|CVE-A,CVE-B|4|31" "alpine:3.10" "2.0"

    # --- QA F-4: currency. `groups > 0 and total > 0` proves ENUMERATION, not
    #     CURRENCY. The scan runs --severity CRITICAL,HIGH, so HIGHs carry
    #     `total` past that guard while the CRITICAL answer can be absent
    #     because the DB is too old to know. Each case below is byte-identical
    #     to 5c on the two base rows — only the control differs.
    run_case "control reports ZERO criticals -> 11 (not 10)" 11 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||5|61
alpine:3.10|0||4|31" "alpine:3.10" "2.0" "$CURRENCY_LINE"

    run_case "control was never scanned -> 11 (not 10)" 11 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||5|61" "alpine:3.10" "2.0" "$CURRENCY_LINE"

    run_case "vulnerability DB older than the limit -> 11 (not 10)" 11 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||5|61
alpine:3.10|7|CVE-A,CVE-B|4|31" "alpine:3.10" "999.0" "$CURRENCY_LINE"

    run_case "DB age unreadable -> 11 (not 10)" 11 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||5|61
alpine:3.10|7|CVE-A,CVE-B|4|31" "alpine:3.10" "" "$CURRENCY_LINE"

    # QA F-6. An EMPTY reference image must NOT reach 10. Both control arms
    #    were guarded on `reference_image` being truthy, so an empty one made
    #    the control vanish and this exact input printed
    #    "reported None CRITICAL" on its way to a CLEARED verdict.
    run_case "EMPTY reference image -> 11 (not 10) — an absent control is not a passed one" 11 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||5|61" "" "2.0" "$CURRENCY_LINE"

    # QA F-14. Case 2 was CHANGED for QA F-4 (it now carries a working control),
    #    and the bare input it was changed FOR — a clean-looking clearance with
    #    no control at all — was left with no case of its own. This is it, and
    #    it is the same rows as case 2 minus the control: the difference between
    #    the two cases is the whole of F-4.
    # QA F-6: this case asserted the EXIT CODE ALONE while its siblings also
    # assert a verdict line. Exit 11 is reachable from SEVERAL refusals, so the
    # code alone does not prove which one fired.
    #
    # Worth stating precisely, because assuming otherwise was my first attempt:
    # this case does NOT refuse on currency. Its input carries a critical CVE on
    # node:24-alpine, so it refuses as UNEXPECTED CRITICAL and never reaches the
    # currency arm — asserting CURRENCY_LINE here would have been wrong and the
    # self-test said so. It asserts its OWN marker.
    run_case "case 2's BARE input, no control args at all -> 11 (not 10)" 11 \
"node:24-alpine|0|CVE-2026-00001|3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||3|40" "" "" "VERDICT: UNEXPECTED CRITICAL"

    # ── QA F-5: a FUTURE DB timestamp ────────────────────────────────────────
    #    NOTE the asserted string. Every INDETERMINATE arm prints the same
    #    CURRENCY_LINE marker, so asserting the marker here CANNOT discriminate:
    #    with the future arm deleted, "future" parses as unreadable, the age
    #    falls to -1, and the could-not-be-read arm prints the identical marker.
    #    Measured — the first version of this case stayed green through TWO
    #    separate reverts. It asserts the sentence only the future arm emits.
    #    The clamp made a future stamp print as "0.0h old" INSIDE a cleared
    #    verdict — the freshest possible reading produced by the one input
    #    meaning the clock cannot be trusted. These two are the pair: the same
    #    rows that CLEAR on a good age must REFUSE on a future one.
    run_case "a FUTURE db timestamp on an otherwise-clearing run -> 11, not a clearance" 11 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||3|40
alpine:3.10|7|CVE-A,CVE-B|4|31" "alpine:3.10" "future" "timestamp is in the FUTURE"

    run_case "POSITIVE CONTROL — the SAME rows with a readable age still clear -> 10" 10 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|0||3|40
alpine:3.10|7|CVE-A,CVE-B|4|31" "alpine:3.10" "2.0" "VERDICT: THE RESIDUAL CLEARED"

    #     NEGATIVE CONTROL for the four above — the currency control must not be
    #     able to red a run that is NOT claiming a clearance. Same control
    #     failure (zero criticals), but the residual is still present, so the
    #     verdict is status quo and the gate stays quiet.
    run_case "a failed control does NOT red the status-quo verdict -> 0" 0 \
"node:24-alpine|0||3|22
postgres:15-alpine|1|CVE-2025-68121|5|61
alpine:3.10|0||4|31" "alpine:3.10" "2.0"

    # 6. The base list here must match refresh-base-images.sh, or a base added
    #    there would silently go unscanned by this gate.
    echo "=== self-test: base list is in step with refresh-base-images.sh ==="
    if [ -f "$REFRESH_SCRIPT" ]; then
        local theirs ours
        # `|| true` is load-bearing: under `set -euo pipefail`, a RENAMED or
        # reshaped LOCAL_BASES makes grep exit 1, pipefail propagates it and
        # errexit kills the script mid-section — no FAIL line, no diff, and the
        # RETURN trap never fires so the tempdir leaks. Peter measured exactly
        # that (exit 1, output ending at the section header). Letting it yield
        # an EMPTY string sends it to the existing empty-vs-ours comparison,
        # which reports FAIL and exits 12 like every other drift.
        theirs="$(sed -n '/^LOCAL_BASES=(/,/^)/p' "$REFRESH_SCRIPT" | grep -oE '"[^"]+"' | tr -d '"' | sort || true)"
        ours="$(printf '%s\n' "${BASES[@]}" | sort)"
        if [ "$theirs" = "$ours" ]; then
            echo "  PASS  base lists identical ($(printf '%s\n' "${BASES[@]}" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') images)"
        else
            echo "  FAIL  base lists differ:"
            diff <(printf '%s\n' "$theirs") <(printf '%s\n' "$ours") | sed 's/^/          /' || true
            fails=$((fails + 1))
        fi
    else
        echo "  FAIL  refresh-base-images.sh not found at $REFRESH_SCRIPT"
        fails=$((fails + 1))
    fi

    # 7. QA F-3. Case 6 proves list A equals list B; it does NOT prove either
    #    matches the STACK. Derive every base actually referenced in the tree
    #    and require each to be gated or explicitly excluded — so a base added
    #    anywhere fails loudly instead of going unscanned in silence.
    echo "=== self-test: every base in the tree is gated or explicitly excluded ==="
    if [ -d "$DEV_DIR" ]; then
        local discovered known unlisted
        # FROM lines (build bases, ${REGISTRY_PREFIX} stripped) + compose image:
        # refs. Stage aliases (`FROM base`, `FROM builder`) carry no tag and are
        # dropped by the `:` filter.
        # QA F-7 WIDENED THE DERIVATION. The guarantee this case states is "a base
        # added ANYWHERE cannot go unscanned in silence", and the old sweep did
        # not earn that word: Dockerfiles only under $DEV_DIR, and compose only
        # at two fixed paths. It missed systemTest/performance/docker/k6/
        # Dockerfile and every nested compose file (observability/,
        # systemTest/akto/, deployments/staging/, the openapi-examples
        # override). Measured: the old sweep derived 11 images, the widened one
        # 27. Rather than narrow the sentence, the sweep now matches it.
        #
        # QA F-9: this said 28. It is 27, and 27 is exactly
        # `BASES ∪ EXCLUDED_BASES` (6 + 21, no overlap) — which is the point of
        # the case below: every derived image must be accounted for in one list
        # or the other. If 28 had been right the case would FAIL, so the comment
        # and the assertion disagreed and only one of them runs.
        #
        # QA F-14 — this comment credited the wrong filter. What excludes a
        # COMMENTED-OUT image line is the `^[[:space:]]*image:` ANCHOR in the
        # grep above: a commented line begins with `#`, so `image:` is not at
        # the start and the anchor never matches it. The `grep -v` that follows
        # is defence in depth for the same case, not the mechanism. The example
        # is real either way: systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml:387 carries
        # nginx:1.27-alpine behind a `#`, and it read as an ungated runtime
        # nginx until the line was actually opened.
        discovered="$(
            {
                find "$REPO_ROOT" -name 'Dockerfile*' -not -path '*/node_modules/*' -print0 2>/dev/null |
                    xargs -0 grep -hoE '^FROM[[:space:]]+[^ ]+' 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}'
                find "$REPO_ROOT" -name 'docker-compose*.yml' -not -path '*/node_modules/*' -print0 2>/dev/null |
                    xargs -0 grep -hE '^[[:space:]]*image:' 2>/dev/null |
                    grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' |
                    grep -oE 'image:[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z0-9${}_./-]+:[A-Za-z0-9._-]+' |
                    sed 's/image:[[:space:]]*//'
            } | sed 's/^\${REGISTRY_PREFIX}//' | grep ':' | grep -v '^\${' | sort -u || true
        )"
        known="$(printf '%s\n' "${BASES[@]}" "${EXCLUDED_BASES[@]}" | sort -u)"
        unlisted="$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$discovered") <(printf '%s\n' "$known") || true)"
        if [ -z "$discovered" ]; then
            # A derivation that finds nothing is a broken derivation, not a pass
            # — the same vacuous-green shape this gate exists to refuse.
            echo "  FAIL  derived NO bases from the tree — the scan of Dockerfiles/compose is broken"
            fails=$((fails + 1))
        elif [ -z "$unlisted" ]; then
            echo "  PASS  all $(printf '%s\n' "$discovered" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') discovered bases are gated or excluded"
        else
            echo "  FAIL  base(s) in the tree that are neither gated nor excluded:"
            printf '%s\n' "$unlisted" | sed 's/^/          /'
            echo "          Add to BASES (plus LOCAL_BASES in refresh-base-images.sh) or to"
            echo "          EXCLUDED_BASES with a reason. Being on neither is what this catches."
            fails=$((fails + 1))
        fi
    else
        echo "  FAIL  Dev directory not found at $DEV_DIR"
        fails=$((fails + 1))
    fi

    if [ "$fails" -ne 0 ]; then
        echo "SELF-TEST FAILED ($fails) — do not trust this gate until it is fixed."
        return 12
    fi
    echo "SELF-TEST PASSED — the gate fails on every known-bad input above."
    return 0
}

# --- main ---------------------------------------------------------------------
MODE="full"
case "${1:-}" in
    --self-test) MODE="self-test" ;;
    --scan-only) MODE="scan-only" ;;
    "") ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option '$1' (allowed: --self-test, --scan-only)" >&2; exit 64 ;;
esac

if [ "$MODE" = "self-test" ]; then
    self_test
    exit $?
fi

command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "docker is required" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -f "$REFRESH_SCRIPT" ] || { echo "refresh-base-images.sh not found at $REFRESH_SCRIPT" >&2; exit 2; }

# Run the gate's own self-test first. A gate that has silently stopped
# discriminating should not be allowed to report a green.
self_test || exit 12
echo

if [ "$MODE" = "full" ]; then
    echo "=== Pull (delegated to refresh-base-images.sh local) ==="
    # Reusing the existing pull leg on purpose — it owns the digest before/after
    # reporting, and a stale local image is this watch's own documented trap.
    bash "$REFRESH_SCRIPT" local
    echo
fi

echo "=== Scan + gate ($TRIVY_IMAGE) ==="
REPORT="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$REPORT"' EXIT

for img in "${BASES[@]}"; do
    json="$(docker run --rm \
        -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
        -v secuura-trivy-cache:/root/.cache \
        "$TRIVY_IMAGE" image --quiet --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --format json "$img" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$json" ]; then
        echo "  $img: SCAN PRODUCED NO OUTPUT — treating as a broken run, not a clean one."
        echo "$img|1|SCAN_FAILED|0|0" >> "$REPORT"
        continue
    fi
    printf '%s' "$json" | analyse_json "$img" "$REPORT"
done

# --- QA F-4: the currency control, scanned in the SAME run with the SAME DB ---
# Not one of BASES: the decide step skips it for findings and reads only its
# CRITICAL count. If this image reports zero criticals the run cannot see
# criticals, and a zero on the baselined image means nothing.
echo "  (currency control) $REFERENCE_IMAGE"
ref_json="$(docker run --rm \
    -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
    -v secuura-trivy-cache:/root/.cache \
    "$TRIVY_IMAGE" image --quiet --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --format json "$REFERENCE_IMAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -n "$ref_json" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$ref_json" | analyse_json "$REFERENCE_IMAGE" "$REPORT"
fi

# The DB age comes from trivy itself, not from a file mtime or a guess. `trivy
# version --format json` reports VulnerabilityDB.UpdatedAt for the cache this
# very run used. Unreadable is NOT treated as fresh — decide() takes an empty
# value as unknown and refuses to call a residual cleared on it.
DB_AGE_HOURS="$(docker run --rm -v secuura-trivy-cache:/root/.cache "$TRIVY_IMAGE" \
    version --format json 2>/dev/null \
  | python3 -c '
import json,sys,datetime,re
try:
    d = json.load(sys.stdin)
    ts = (d.get("VulnerabilityDB") or {}).get("UpdatedAt")
    if not ts:
        print(""); raise SystemExit
    ts = ts.replace("Z", "+00:00")
    # QA F-8. trivy stamps RFC3339 with NANOSECOND precision. On a host running
    # python < 3.11 `fromisoformat` rejects that outright, so this whole block
    # raised, printed "", and decide() read the age as unknown — which makes the
    # gate PERMANENTLY indeterminate the moment a residual clears, silently
    # disabling the one verdict it exists to produce. It fails safe, which is
    # why nothing noticed. Truncate the fraction to microseconds first.
    ts = re.sub(r"\.(\d{6})\d+", r".\1", ts)
    upd = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(ts)
    now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
    age = (now - upd).total_seconds() / 3600
    # QA F-5. A FUTURE stamp (clock skew, a bad cache) was CLAMPED to 0 and then
    # printed inside a CLEARED verdict as "the vulnerability DB is 0.0h old" —
    # i.e. the freshest possible reading, produced by the one input that means
    # the clock cannot be trusted at all. That is the worst direction for this
    # value to fail in: it is the sentence an operator reads before running the
    # ACR leg against the live registry.
    #
    # A future stamp is now its OWN answer. It is not "fresh" and it is not
    # "stale" — it is unreadable, and decide() must say INDETERMINATE with a
    # remedy that fits a clock rather than one that says re-download the DB.
    if age < 0:
        print("future")
    else:
        print(f"{age:.2f}")
except Exception:
    print("")
' 2>/dev/null || true)"
[ -n "$DB_AGE_HOURS" ] && echo "  (currency control) vulnerability DB age: ${DB_AGE_HOURS}h (limit ${MAX_DB_AGE_HOURS}h)" \
                      || echo "  (currency control) vulnerability DB age: UNREADABLE"

echo
echo "Baseline: $BASELINE_IMAGE / $BASELINE_CVE (the one tolerated residual — see the header)."
echo
decide "$REPORT" "$REFERENCE_IMAGE" "$DB_AGE_HOURS" "$MAX_DB_AGE_HOURS"
